prompt:
Add a maintained, instance-local URL transformation option throughout markdown-it's built-in resource parsing. Applications need to proxy or rewrite Markdown link and image destinations according to the current render environment while keeping labels, reference reuse, parser plugins and existing URL validation intact. Implement the feature across the option API, inline and core parsing paths, tests, documentation and an executable example. Edit maintained source and rebuild the distributable entry points.

Public API: new MarkdownIt({urlTransform}) and md.set({urlTransform}) accept a function, null or undefined. Null/undefined disable transformation. Other values synchronously throw TypeError mentioning urlTransform; an invalid set call must leave all previous options unchanged. Keep set fluent, presets usable, and independent instances isolated.

Invoke the function as urlTransform.call(md, url, info), where url is the original destination after the existing normalizeLink and validateLink checks. info is a fresh object per callback with kind ('link' or 'image'), source ('inline', 'reference', 'autolink' or 'linkify'), and env (the exact environment object for that parse/render). Return undefined to preserve the normalized original destination, or a string to replace it, including an empty string. Normalize and validate replacement strings with the instance's current normalizeLink and validateLink methods. A replacement rejected by validateLink, or any return value other than a string/undefined (including null, a Promise or another thenable), synchronously throws TypeError mentioning urlTransform. Propagate callback-thrown values unchanged, including null, zero and object identity. A failed or reentrant render must not corrupt the next render's policy or environment. Do not install per-render state on shared instances, prototypes or globals.

Cover every built-in resource-producing path: inline links/images, full/collapsed/shortcut references, URL and email autolinks, and both scheme-based and fuzzy/email linkification. Call once for each resource token actually generated by the built-in rules, including nested resource tokens in image children; silent speculative parsing must not call the hook. Reference definitions remain normalized original metadata, the callback runs independently at each use, and unused definitions do not invoke it. Existing rejection of an unsafe original URL happens before the callback. Raw HTML, inline/fenced code and tokens inserted directly by application plugins are outside this option's scope.

The transformed URL must be present on normal Token href/src attributes as soon as parse or parseInline returns, so custom renderers work without special APIs. render/renderInline and built CommonJS/browser bundles must expose the same behavior. Preserve nesting, title/alt/label formatting, displayed autolink/linkified text, existing HTML escaping, parser rule enable/disable behavior and ordinary output when the option is disabled. The callback receives the current environment even across sequential renders with different environments, reference reuse, separate instances and a callback that reenters the same MarkdownIt instance.

Add focused regression tests across the public configuration and parsing/rendering APIs, all resource syntax paths, silent probing, reference reuse, invalid options/results, thrown values, URL validation, plugin interoperability and reentrant isolation. Document the API and provide a runnable proxying example. Run the original project suite, npm run lint, npm run build and the example; repair new regressions and finish with accurate implementation and validation results. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.
